result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
Your worry doesn't hold up. None of the three open Transformer 1 work orders has a technician or a scheduled date, and none is overdue. So nothing was reassigned. The real risk is that Transformer 1 is at Condition 4 and its urgent work isn't staffed or scheduled.

**1. MAIN work order KPIs, last 6 months**
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total work orders | 3 (all Priority 1, all on Transformer 1) |
| Completed | 0 |
| Backlog | 3 |
| Overdue | 0 |
| Average completion time | 0 hrs (reported as 0 because nothing has been completed) |

**2. Open work orders on Transformer 1**
| WO # | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled date | Technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000053 | Outage + inspection Transformer 1 (C57.104 Cond 4) | 1 | WAPPR (awaiting approval) | None | None | No |
| 1000052 | Confirmatory DGA oil sample, Transformer 1 | 1 | APPR (approved) | None | None | No |
| 1000051 | Inspection of the on-load tap changer (OLTC) for suspected contact wear/coking | 1 | APPR (approved) | None | None | No |

All three were raised today (2026-09-30). The notes on 1000053 and 1000051 mention target dates in January 2024, but these were never entered as scheduled or target dates. They're also out of date and should be replaced.

**3. Technician workload**
No technicians are assigned to these work orders, so there was no one to count and no one is overloaded. There is also no one at MAIN with past work on Transformer 1: the asset has only these 3 work orders, all unassigned. The note on 1000051 says the same.

**4. TDCG, latest oil sample (2024-01-19)**
- Hydrogen 2850 + methane 7400 + ethane 5470 + ethylene 16650 + acetylene 7 + CO 32 = **32,409 ppm**
- That is **Condition 4** (above 4630).
- All six gases were present, so none was carried forward.
- This sample is about 2.7 years old. It's the newest data in the system.

**5. Reassignment decision**
Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, so the reassignment rule applies. But no work order qualifies: none is overdue and none sits with an overloaded technician. I made no changes.

The no-history rule doesn't technically apply either, because no one has Transformer 1 history at all, overloaded or not. The practical conclusion is the same: there is no least-loaded in-house technician to name, and you should **bring in outside or specialist transformer help**.

**Suggestions for getting the work moving:**
1. Approve 1000053 and replace the January 2024 outage dates in its notes with a current window.
2. Assign someone, internal or contracted, and schedule the work in this order: 1000052 (confirmatory oil sample) first, then 1000051 (tap changer inspection) and 1000053 (outage + inspection) together in one outage.
3. The schedule is clear. MAIN has 0 work orders scheduled from 2026-10-01 to 10-07, so any day in the next week stays under the 3-per-day limit. 2026-10-01 is the earliest option.
4. Before acting on the 2024 sample, get a fresh oil sample (1000052). Condition 4 normally means notifying the manufacturer and considering taking the unit out of service.
